definition: Using a model to write, critique, or optimize prompts for itself or other models, including automated prompt-optimization loops (DSPy-style) that treat prompts as tunable parameters.
details: Using a model to write, critique, or optimize prompts for itself or other models, including automated prompt-optimization loops (DSPy-style) that treat prompts as tunable parameters.

explainer.lead: Meta-prompting uses a model to write, critique, or optimize prompts for itself or other models, including automated prompt-optimization loops that treat prompts as tunable parameters. It matters because it turns prompt design into something that can be searched and improved automatically.

tiers.eli5: It is like asking a writer to edit their own instructions before starting, then checking the result and editing again. The instructions get better without you rewriting them by hand.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers set up loops where a model drafts a prompt, critiques it, and revises, or where DSPy-style optimization treats the prompt as a parameter to tune. The pitfall is that the loop optimizes against whatever feedback it is given, so a weak critique signal yields a confidently bad prompt.
tiers.paperLevel: Using a model to write, critique, or optimize prompts for itself or other models, including automated prompt-optimization loops (DSPy-style) that treat prompts as tunable parameters. Quality is bounded by the critique or scoring signal that drives the loop.

explainer.example: A pipeline has the model rewrite its own instruction, scores the outputs on a validation set, and keeps the prompt version with the best score.
